about: Stages and timing for the voice-of-customer playbook. scripts/handoff.py reads this file: the stages it tracks, the outcomes each stage can record, and how long to wait between stages. Each key is explained under notes.

stages.name: listen
stages.do: Read the survey's scores, answers and trend with how far to trust them, add what to act on (detractors, unhappy customers, a failing step) as findings, and ask the user which to follow up.

stages.name: segment
stages.do: Define and size the follow-up audience from the survey answers (for example detractors), with the consent the follow-up's channel needs, and reuse or create it after its own yes.

skip_when.reason: the listen stage found nothing to follow up, or too few answers to trust.

stages.name: flow
stages.do: Build a draft follow-up flow triggered by the survey answer, after its own yes; or record that the user prefers a one-off email to the audience.

skip_when.reason: the listen stage found nothing to follow up, or too few answers to trust.
no follow-up audience was made, so there is no one for a flow to follow up.

stages.name: test
stages.do: Optionally add an A/B split to the draft flow after its own yes (for example a holdout that gets no follow-up), before QA so QA sees the split; record no_test, or skip the stage, when the user doesn't want a test.

skip_when.reason: the listen stage found nothing to follow up, or too few answers to trust.
no follow-up flow was built, so there is no flow to test.
the flow stage was skipped, so there is no flow to test.

stages.name: qa-flow
stages.do: QA the draft flow, with its A/B split if the test stage added one, until it is GO; a NO-GO fix goes back through the flow stage's write skill (engagement-scenario-builder), with its own yes, and is QA'd again. Then wait for the user to switch it on in the Engagement UI, record the day it started, and record the switch-on as a change (source engagement-ui).

skip_when.reason: the listen stage found nothing to follow up, or too few answers to trust.
no follow-up flow was built.
the flow stage was skipped, so there is no flow to QA.

stages.name: email
stages.do: Draft a one-off follow-up email to the audience, after its own yes; never scheduled or sent.

skip_when.reason: the listen stage found nothing to follow up, or too few answers to trust.
a follow-up flow was built instead of an email.
the user chose no follow-up flow and no email.
no follow-up audience was made, so there is no one to email.

stages.name: qa-email
stages.do: QA the email draft until it is GO; a NO-GO fix is made by the user in the HTML editor or by a new draft from the email stage's write skill (engagement-email-builder). Then wait for the user to schedule it in the Engagement UI, and record the send as a change (source engagement-ui).

skip_when.reason: no email draft was made.
the email stage was skipped, so there is no email to QA.

stages.name: ab-read-out
stages.do: Read out the test stage's split on its agreed primary metric: call the winner, keep it running until a later date, or stop as inconclusive. The user acts on the verdict in the Engagement UI.

skip_when.reason: the listen stage found nothing to follow up, or too few answers to trust.
the flow was never switched on.
there is no live flow, so there is no test to read out.
no A/B split was added, so there is no test to read out.
the test stage was skipped, so there is no test to read out.

stages.name: recheck
stages.do: Read the same survey again with the same question and scoring: did the score, the detractor share or the answer that started the run move since the follow-up went live?

skip_when.reason: the listen stage found nothing to follow up, or too few answers to trust.
no follow-up went live.
no follow-up went live.
no follow-up went live.
no follow-up went live.

notes.recheck_after_days: Days after the follow-up went live before the recheck is due. engagement-survey-insights reads a 90-day window by default and needs min_responses answers to trust a score; about 60 days gives eight or more weekly points after the follow-up, enough for its weekly trend. The recheck counts from whichever QA stage ran (qa-flow or qa-email; not_before lists both and counts from the latest one done).
notes.readout_after_days: Days after the flow started (the qa-flow stage's done date) before the ab-read-out stage is due. engagement-ab-test-setup sizes a test in whole weeks and never below its min_test_days, which engagement-experiment-readout uses too; 14 matches that minimum. When the test stage agreed a later end date, the readout says keep running: record keep_running with that date.
notes.wait_outcomes: Outcomes that mean a stage isn't finished yet. The script records them only with status in_progress and a --not-before date to come back on, so status never shows the stage as due before then. no_clear_change is the way out when the survey never collects enough answers. keep_running is the ab-read-out stage's wait, when the test needs more customers or days; inconclusive is its way out when the test never reaches its sample.
notes.playbooks: Each playbook's title, product and stages in order. A stage names the skill that does it, whether that skill writes, what to do, the outcomes it can record, not_before (wait this rules key's number of days after another stage is done) and skip_when (suggest skipping when another stage had one of these outcomes, or with skipped: true when it was skipped; all means every condition must hold; skips don't cascade). The follow-up is either a flow (engagement-scenario-builder, QA'd by scenario-qa) or a one-off email (engagement-email-builder, QA'd by campaign-qa): the flow stage's outcome picks the path, and status offers the other path's stages as skips. not_built on the flow stage means the user wants neither a flow nor an email, so the email stage is offered as a skip too; not_created on the segment stage means there is no audience to follow up, so both the flow and the email stages are offered as skips. The flow uses engagement-scenario-builder rather than scenario-template-launcher: a survey follow-up isn't one of the lifecycle flows the launcher clones, and the builder builds a draft from an outline. The recheck reads the survey before and after; it isn't a test. On the flow path, the optional test stage (engagement-ab-test-setup) adds an A/B split to the draft before qa-flow, so scenario-qa checks the split too, for example a holdout that compares following up against not following up; it records its write from its plan and verify files. When the user doesn't want a test, or takes the email path, the test stage is skipped and status then offers ab-read-out (engagement-experiment-readout) as a skip. ab-read-out reads the split out before the recheck.
